8dff467cd0aa1fe7: JAKARTA: Pihak berkuasa Indonesia merampas 1.16 tan ketamin daripada sebuah kapal tangki dipintas di luar perairan Wilayah Sumatera Utara dan menahan lapan anak kapal menerusi satu operasi bersepadu, kata pegawai kanan polis pada Jumaat, lapor Xinhua.

Ketua Unit Siasatan Narkotik Polis Nasional, Suyudi Ario Seto, berkata pihak berkuasa memintas kapal tangki MT Global 168 di luar perairan Tanjung Balai Asahan, selepas hampir seminggu menjalankan pemantauan membabitkan polis, Badan Narkotik Kebangsaan, kastam dan polis marin.

Ketika berucap di Pelabuhan Bandar Deli di Medan, Suyudi berkata, pihak berkuasa mula menjejaki kapal itu pada 14 Okt lalu, ketika ia belayar melalui perairan berhampiran Malaysia sebelum menuju ke utara Aceh dan Thailand.
Pihak penyiasat mengesan kejanggalan dalam sistem pengenalan automatik kapal itu yang memaparkan dua nama berbeza, iaitu MT Global dan Gross Dolphin, katanya.

Pegawai penguat kuasa menahan tujuh anak kapal warga Indonesia dan seorang warga asing, selain merampas 58 guni yang mengandungi keseluruhan 1.16 tan ketamin bersama peralatan komunikasi dan kapal tangki itu.
5e49a1065a81c641: KUALA LUMPUR: Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah's late-season resurgence gathered further momentum on Friday as they booked a French Open semi-final spot, putting them another step closer to a first back-to-back World Tour title double.
The world No. 4 pair brushed aside Bulgaria's Gabriela Stoeva-Stefani Stoeva 21-12, 21-15 in just 39 minutes to reach their second semi-final in as many weeks.
Fresh from their Denmark Open triumph last Sunday, the second seeds have yet to drop a game in Paris despite the physical demands of a hectic tournament schedule.
Their latest victory was another encouraging sign after an inconsistent middle stretch of the season, which saw them suffer early exits at several major tournaments.
Although they reached the Taiwan Open final in July and claimed Asian Games bronze last month, Pearly-Thinaah struggled to reproduce the form that brought them three World Tour titles last year.
However, Pearly believes the past two weeks have helped restore their confidence following injury setbacks.
"After the injury, we've been doing well these two weeks. I'm very happy that we've regained our momentum and confidence," she said in a post-match interview with the Badminton World Federation.
"We're enjoying ourselves on court and trusting each other. Our bond on court is very strong."
Pearly was equally pleased with their patience against the Bulgarian sisters, although she admitted they had occasionally rushed their play.
"We did a lot of discussion, and I think we did well with our patience. Towards the end, we were rushing a little, but we kept reminding each other and managed to get back on track," she said.
Their victory extended their head-to-head advantage over the Stoeva sisters to 5-1.
Standing between them and another final are Japan's third seeds, Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakanishi, who defeated compatriots Ririna Hiramoto-Chiharu Shida 21-18, 16-21, 21-15.
The Malaysians hold an 8-2 advantage over the Japanese pair, having won their last four meetings, including the Arctic Open and Kumamoto Masters finals last year.
Despite that encouraging record, Thinaah stressed that recovery would be crucial ahead of Saturday's semi-final.
"Mentally and physically, we need to be well prepared, especially with our recovery," she said.
"We're grateful to have our mentor and physio with us. They've been helping us a lot with our recovery."
Pearly-Thinaah, who captured their breakthrough French Open title in 2022, have won multiple World Tour titles in a season but have never triumphed at consecutive tournaments.
666feb89e39b4bae: PETALING JAYA: There must be an in-depth study to determine how the recent F1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Sepang generated RM950 million in economic activity before Putrajaya makes it a regular event, experts say.

Sunway University economist Yeah Kim Leng said Malaysia must first determine how much of the money spent during the Oct 2-4 race weekend came from foreign visitors who travelled specifically to attend the F1 race.
He pointed out that part of the economic contribution would have come from Malaysians who would otherwise have spent their money elsewhere, whether on holidays or other leisure activities.
Universiti Teknologi Mara tourism management lecturer Hafiz Hanafiah said the spending that really counts is that by foreign visitors.
To illustrate his point, Hafiz used the analogy of a bathtub.
“Think of the Malaysian economy as a bathtub,” he told FMT. He explained that the amount of water in the bathtub only increases when more water is poured into it.
“If a Malaysian skips a trip to Langkawi to buy an F1 ticket, he is just moving the water from one end of the tub to the other. It may look busy, but the water level doesn’t rise,” he said.
On that score alone, he added, spending by foreigners would be needed to give the Malaysian economy a boost.
Last week, youth and sports minister Taufik Johari announced that the Bahrain F1 generated US$232 million — the equivalent of RM950 million — for Malaysia.
A total of 261,000 spectators filled the stands over the three days. In addition, Taufik said, the event attracted more than 50,000 foreign visitors to Malaysia.
He added that the government was considering the prospect of hosting F1 races every few years in partnership with another country, rather than holding such events annually.
However, he said the proposal was still “at an early stage” and that a report on the costs and benefits was expected by the end of November.

Hafiz also pointed out that even if Malaysia played host only once every few years, each event would have to generate at least RM300 million in additional revenue from foreign tourists to justify the effort.
Even so, that amount would only cover the hosting fee payable to Liberty Media, which holds the F1 commercial rights.

For the recent F1 race in Sepang, Bahrain paid the hosting fee, allowing Malaysia to benefit from tourism spending without any upfront financial outlay. In return, Hafiz pointed out, Bahrain collected all the ticket revenue.
Yeah pointed out that this arrangement would not apply to future events if Malaysia decided to play host again.
Rope in private sector, extend duration
Hafiz said the government could bring in private businesses to sponsor the event and defray the cost of hosting the F1, as Singapore had done.
He also suggested extending F1-related events over a 10-day period and taking them to other parts of the country to encourage tourists to stay longer and, consequently, spend more.

But Yeah also offered a word of caution. He said Putrajaya should first determine whether the RM300 million needed to host the race would be better spent on other public needs, such as schools and hospitals.
“The same funds could address more immediate economic priorities,” he said.

Yeah said hosting the race occasionally rather than annually would reduce government spending while keeping public interest high. However, money would still have to be spent on the regular maintenance of the Sepang International Circuit.
According to Hafiz, that sum could be as high as RM10 million a year to maintain the circuit at F1 standards.
619df372b1d8dbf4: PETALING JAYA: Few woods are as prized for their scent as gaharu. Rich, smoky and intensely fragrant, it has been used for centuries in perfume, incense and religious traditions - and the finest pieces can command extraordinary prices.

But gaharu does not come from just any tree. In Malaysia, it is produced by several species including "Aquilaria malaccensis", a native tree whose resin-rich wood forms after the plant is wounded, infected by fungi or otherwise stressed.

That rarity is part of what makes gaharu valuable, but it has also placed wild trees under considerable pressure. According to Malaysia’s biodiversity database, demand for agarwood - the international name for gaharu - continues to exceed supply, while illegal harvesting remains a threat to wild populations of "A malaccensis".

Now, researchers and fragrance companies are exploring whether artificial intelligence and biotechnology could help reproduce some of the scents traditionally obtained from rare plants without repeatedly harvesting them.

According to a recent report in The Guardian, companies are using AI to analyse the relationship between molecules and the scents people perceive. One of these firms, Osmo, is developing systems that can predict how particular molecules will smell and help identify substitutes for difficult-to-source natural ingredients.

In one case, the company reportedly reproduced the scent of a rare tree after receiving only a small sample of bark. Other biotechnology firms are taking a different approach, growing plant cells in laboratories so fragrance compounds can be produced without repeatedly cutting material from wild plants.

Agarwood is among the ingredients attracting interest because of the pressure created by global demand. The scent comes from resin that develops inside certain trees, rather than from ordinary healthy wood, which makes high-quality natural gaharu relatively scarce.

Peninsular Malaysia is home to five recognised "Aquilaria" species, according to the forestry department, including "A malaccensis", "A hirta" and "A microcarpa". The department notes that gaharu forms when the tree responds to fungal infection, injury or pest attack by producing a fragrant oil that eventually hardens into resin.

Malaysia’s biodiversity database lists "A malaccensis" as Critically Endangered and "A hirta", another local source of gaharu, as Vulnerable. International trade in "Aquilaria" species is also regulated under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora.

Plantations have been established to help meet demand, but cultivated trees do not always produce resin with the same qualities as wild sources. That helps explain why naturally produced gaharu can remain especially sought after even when farmed alternatives exist.

The idea of recreating rare scents in a laboratory sounds promising, but researchers and conservationists caution against assuming that synthetic fragrance will automatically protect threatened trees.

As The Guardian reported, demand for authentic natural ingredients may continue even when convincing substitutes become available. Replicating a scent also does nothing by itself to protect forests, stop illegal harvesting or preserve the wider ecosystems in which threatened plants grow.
Still, if AI and biotechnology can supply some of the fragrance compounds currently taken from vulnerable species, they could potentially reduce part of the pressure on wild populations.

For Malaysia’s gaharu trees, that would not replace conservation. But in a market where a rare scent can make a piece of wood enormously valuable, finding ways to create that aroma without cutting down another tree could become one useful part of the solution.
3672bb2f2eb61eb4: PETALING JAYA: Pakar berpendapat kajian mendalam perlu dijalankan bagi menentukan bagaimana Grand Prix Bahrain F1 yang berlangsung di Sepang baru-baru ini menjana aktiviti ekonomi bernilai RM950 juta, sebelum kerajaan menjadikannya acara tetap.

Ahli ekonomi dari Universiti Sunway, Yeah Kim Leng, berkata Malaysia perlu terlebih dahulu mengenal pasti jumlah perbelanjaan sepanjang hujung minggu perlumbaan pada 2 hingga 4 Okt daripada pelancong asing yang datang khusus untuk menyaksikan perlumbaan F1 itu.

Jelasnya, sebahagian daripada sumbangan ekonomi itu mungkin datang daripada rakyat Malaysia sendiri, yang sebaliknya akan membelanjakan wang mereka di tempat lain, sama ada bercuti atau melakukan aktiviti riadah lain.
Pensyarah pengurusan pelancongan di Universiti Teknologi Mara, Hafiz Hanafiah, berkata perbelanjaan yang benar-benar memberi impak ialah perbelanjaan oleh pelancong asing.
Bagi menjelaskan pandangannya, beliau menggunakan analogi tab mandi.
"Bayangkan ekonomi Malaysia seperti sebuah tab mandi," katanya kepada FMT sambil menjelaskan jumlah air di dalam tab mandi hanya akan bertambah apabila lebih banyak air dituang ke dalamnya.

"Jika seorang rakyat Malaysia membatalkan percutian ke Langkawi semata-mata untuk membeli tiket F1, dia sebenarnya hanya memindahkan air dari satu bahagian tab mandi ke bahagian lain. Keadaan mungkin kelihatan sibuk, tetapi paras air tidak meningkat."
Katanya, perbelanjaan pelancong asing amat diperlukan untuk merangsang pertumbuhan ekonomi Malaysia.
Minggu lalu, Menteri Belia dan Sukan, Taufik Johari, mengumumkan Grand Prix Bahrain F1 menjana pendapatan USD232 juta, bersamaan RM950 juta kepada Malaysia.
Seramai 261,000 penonton memenuhi tempat duduk penonton sepanjang tiga hari perlumbaan itu berlangsung. Selain itu, Taufik berkata, acara itu menarik lebih 50,000 pelancong asing ke Malaysia.
Jelasnya, kerajaan sedang mempertimbangkan kemungkinan menganjurkan F1 beberapa tahun sekali, dengan kerjasama negara lain berbanding menganjurkannya setiap tahun.
Tetapi, beliau berkata, cadangan itu masih di "peringkat awal" dan laporan mengenai kos serta manfaat dijangka siap menjelang akhir bulan depan.

Hafiz berkata, walaupun Malaysia hanya menjadi tuan rumah sekali dalam tempoh beberapa tahun, setiap kali penganjuran perlu menjana sekurang-kurangnya RM300 juta hasil tambahan daripada perbelanjaan pelancong asing bagi memastikan ia berbaloi.
Pun begitu, jumlah itu hanya cukup untuk menampung yuran penganjuran yang perlu dibayar kepada Liberty Media, pemegang hak komersial F1.

Bagi perlumbaan F1 di Sepang baru-baru ini, Bahrain telah membayar yuran penganjuran, membolehkan Malaysia meraih manfaat daripada perbelanjaan pelancong tanpa perlu mengeluarkan sebarang kos awal. Sebagai balasan, jelas Hafiz, Bahrain memperoleh semua hasil jualan tiket.
Yeah berkata, aturan ini tidak akan terpakai bagi acara akan datang, jika Malaysia memutuskan untuk menjadi tuan rumah sekali lagi.
Libatkan sektor swasta, lanjut tempoh acara
Hafiz berkata, kerajaan boleh melibatkan syarikat swasta untuk menaja acara itu dan menampung kos penganjuran F1, seperti yang dilakukan Singapura.

Beliau turut mencadangkan acara berkaitan F1 dilanjutkan kepada 10 hari dan diadakan di kawasan lain seluruh negara bagi menggalakkan pelancong tinggal lebih lama dan seterusnya berbelanja lebih banyak.

Namun, Yeah turut memberi peringatan Putrajaya perlu terlebih dahulu menentukan sama ada RM300 juta yang diperlukan untuk menganjurkan perlumbaan itu mungkin lebih baik digunakan bagi keperluan awam lain, seperti sekolah dan hospital.
"Dana yang sama boleh digunakan untuk menangani keutamaan ekonomi lebih mendesak."

Yeah berpendapat, menganjurkan perlumbaan itu sekali-sekala berbanding setiap tahun dapat mengurangkan perbelanjaan kerajaan sambil mengekalkan minat orang ramai. Tetapi, perbelanjaan tetap diperlukan untuk penyelenggaraan berkala Litar Antarabangsa Sepang.
Hafiz berkata, kos menyelenggara litar itu untuk memenuhi piawaian F1 boleh mencecah sehingga RM10 juta setahun.
d85a03415f9af4f5: BUENOS AIRES: A federal judge on Friday dismissed a criminal case against Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister, in which they were accused of promoting a suspected cryptocurrency scam that resulted in at least US$100 million in losses for investors.
"The reported events do not constitute a criminal offence," Judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi said in a ruling reviewed by AFP.
Milei had hailed the $LIBRA meme coin in a social media post in February 2025, saying: "The world wants to invest in Argentina. $LIBRA."
He deleted the post hours later after the currency crashed. Milei later denied promoting the virtual currency, saying he "did not know the details of the project".
Industry experts have called the operation a "rug pull" — a scam in which developers unveil a crypto token, attract investors and then quickly cash out.
The investigation sought to determine whether a coordinated scheme had taken place, with the president's involvement.
Nine other individuals under investigation were also cleared.
The judge wrote that investor losses and the rise and fall in the currency's price were insufficient to establish fraud.

Investigators also found no proof that Karina Milei, the president's right-hand woman who serves as secretary-general of the presidency, had received payments for facilitating meetings between the entrepreneurs behind the virtual currency and her brother.
"Facilitating a contact or helping to organise a meeting does not, in itself, amount to influence peddling," the judge wrote.
de7030a5f0f2e15c: WASHINGTON: The US defence department has designated Chinese-funded cultural centres on university campuses known as Confucius Institutes as a threat to US national security, defence secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday.
Washington has long accused Confucius Institutes of being Chinese propaganda tools and has taken steps to crack down on them.

Hegseth, in a video posted on social media, alleged that Confucius Institutes were operating under disguise at US universities and that the Pentagon had added them to its list of institutions that threaten US national security.

"It turns out that 80 new propaganda cells across 30 universities had popped up using different names and different charters, but with the same mission: to steal intellectual property and to infiltrate the minds of American students," Hegseth said.
The defence department over the past two months has "systematically dismantled every single one of these organisations," he said.
The Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
3d76501e29ba63bd: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for the country's army companies to be turned into elite, self-sufficient combat units during a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media KCNA said on Saturday.
The event underscored Kim's consistent policy priority of strengthening the military.

In a speech at a conference of company commanders for North Korea's army on Oct 22-23, which KCNA said was the first military-wide gathering since the Ninth Congress of North Korea's ruling party in February, Kim called for every company to be fully prepared so that "the goal of the new-era military build-up" could be achieved.
"Let us build the strongest army and speed up a military revolution in our style," Kim said.

During the Ninth Congress of North Korea's ruling party in February, which sets the country's direction for the next five years, Kim called for stronger conventional armed forces while reaffirming efforts to develop nuclear weapons and missiles.
c616d7feec6f38e7: PETALING JAYA: Four Malaysian doubles pairs have secured semi-final spots at the French Open badminton championships after winning their quarter-final matches.
This is a record achievement at the prestigious BWF World Tour Super 750 championships.

And history beckons for world No 4 Pearly Tan-M Thinaah, who could add a second title being the only Malaysian women’s doubles pair to have won the crown in the tournament’s 117-year history, in 2022.

In the last eight match early this morning, the Malaysian pair defeated world No 9 pair Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva-Stefani Stoeva with a comfortable score of 21-12, 21-15 in a match that took 39 minutes.
In the semi-final, the newly-crowned Denmark Open champions will take on Japan’s world No 5 Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakashini, who they have beaten eight times in their 10 encounters so far.

Men’s doubles world No 5 pair Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzudin Rumsani shocked South Korea’s world No 1 pair Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae in just 36 minutes, winning 21-15, 21-18. It's the Malaysians' third win out of seven clashes against the Koreans.
They will face Indonesia’s world No 25 pair Leo Rolly Carnando-Daniel Marthin in the semi-finals. The Malaysian pair have the edge on paper having beaten them twice in as many encounters.

The other men's doubles semi-finals will feature Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun who had an easy path to the last four after being given a walkover by their higher-ranked compatriots Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik in the quarter-final.
The world No 4 duo retired while trailing 0-5 in just two minutes into the first game. No official reasons have been given for their withdrawal.

Wei Chong-Kai Wun, ranked world No 11, will meet Indonesian pair Raymond Indra-Nikolaus Joaquin, who are ranked three spots below them. The two pairs have met only once before, with the Indonesians winning the encounter.
Malaysia will be hoping to end the 22-year wait for a men’s doubles title, which was last won by Gan Teik Chai-Koo Kien Keat in 2004.

In the mixed doubles, played earlier, where a Malaysian pair has never won the title since the tournament’s inception in 1909, there is now a ray of hope with Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing who beat higher-ranked pairs in their earlier matches.
They have to overcome China’s world No 6 pair Guo Xin Wai-Chen Fang Hui in the semi-final today if they aspire to achieve the feat.
137b43444551aec7: KUALA LUMPUR: A post-mortem on a 42-year-old man who died in police custody found no internal organ injuries, although several external injuries were detected.
Bukit Aman Integrity and Standards Compliance Department director Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid said the cause of death remained pending laboratory analysis.

The man, who was arrested by Cheras police on Sept 19 in connection with investigations under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and Sections 457 and 379 of the Penal Code, was referred to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz on Sept 30 for treatment.
He was given initial treatment by doctors but was pronounced dead at 1.52am on Oct 1.
Aida said the case had been classified as sudden death, with the Death in Custody Criminal Investigation Unit continuing investigations from various angles.

She said the unit had recorded statements from 78 witnesses, including policemen, the public, medical officers, forensic medical specialists, National Legal Aid Foundation representatives and two family members of the deceased.
The case had also been referred to the Independent Police Conduct Commission in accordance with Section 26 of the IPCC Act 2022.
187dded282ab3a33: PARIS: Moody's spared France a credit rating downgrade on Friday, easing pressure on a government struggling to contain social unrest and shore up its strained finances.
Moody's said it had concluded a periodic review of its rating, leaving it at Aa3, which has carried a negative outlook since last October.

Bond markets had been pricing in a downgrade, which would have brought Moody's in line with Standard & Poor's and Fitch, which moved earlier as France struggled to rein in its public finances after a 2024 snap election produced a hung parliament and political paralysis.

The French finance ministry said in a statement that the fact Moody's kept its rating unchanged reflected the "credibility of the budget the government has put forward in the 2027 finance bill, which is designed to keep our public finances on the path to recovery."
The government is struggling to pass the bill in parliament, where opposition parties could refuse to compromise, reject the legislation and topple the government in a no-confidence vote.
"The Aa3 rating assumes that a deficit-reducing budget for 2027 will be adopted, while financing costs and social tensions will abate somewhat in the next few months," Moody's said in a statement.

French borrowing costs already exceed those of lower-rated peers such as Italy, as investors fret over the budget deficit -- one of the eurozone's biggest -- and a presidential election on April 18 and May 2 next year that polls suggest the far right could win.
TV images of weekend protests descending into riots and looting underscore the political difficulty of pushing budget cuts through.

That helped push the risk premium on French government debt over safe-haven German bonds to its highest in 15 years on Thursday, while France's benchmark 10-year bond yield hit 5.14%, its highest level since July 2002.
Moody's said earlier this month that the French government's ability to overcome "fragmentation in parliament" would be the key factor for its next rating move.

That task looks harder after violent protests over underfunded schools escalated last weekend into riots during mass cost-of-living demonstrations. The government has refused to release more school funding or raise the minimum wage, and further protests are planned for Saturday.

In parliament, the lower house has scrapped some key savings measures in the 2027 budget, which targets a deficit of 5% of output versus 5.4% this year. Opposition parties show little appetite for compromise before the election, scrapping some proposed cuts while adding spending.

"You want to wait and see how the narrative evolves over the next six months into the election. That's going to have a more meaningful impact on the spread," said Rushabh Amin, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments.

Pressure on French debt could grow after the presidential vote if Moody's, S&P and Fitch all cut France to BBB -- just above junk status -- potentially forcing sales by those investors with rating limits, said Mike Bell, head of market strategy at RBC BlueBay Asset Management.
"That's where it could really start to get more ugly," he added.
2e146672f5153336: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP and Pakatan Harapan are expected to face an uphill battle in the Melaka polls as a potential Barisan Nasional-Pas electoral pact could consolidate Malay support and replicate the electoral trend seen in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
But political analysts said DAP and PH could still pull off a surprise by winning over young and undecided voters, particularly in mixed constituencies and seats won with narrow margins.

Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities director Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said PH was likely to retain support in five Chinese-majority and mixed-demographic constituencies.
He said support among Chinese and Indian voters, as well as middle-class Malays in urban and semi-urban areas, would be crucial to PH's electoral performance.
"Fundamentally, rural Malay voters remain deeply committed to the Malay-Muslim narrative.
"Conversely, urban Malays and non-Malay voters, particularly the Chinese, prioritise issues such as the cost of living, governance, development and national-level concerns."

He said several national political controversies could influence voter sentiment, including issues involving Tabung Haji, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's donation issue, the political and royal crisis in Negri Sembilan and financial leakages during BN's past administration.
He said these issues could influence young and undecided voters, potentially benefiting PH if they shift support to the coalition.

Despite PH's potential to gain ground, Mazlan said the Malay-Muslim narrative was expected to remain influential among rural Malay voters, giving BN and Pas an advantage in a substantial number of constituencies.
"On paper, BN could win easily. However, in mixed constituencies or areas with narrow margins, the situation could shift, potentially leading to surprises in this state election."
Social media campaigning and the ability to address voters' concerns would be crucial in determining the outcome, he added.
"The party that succeeds in mastering social media and effectively addressing key issues will stand a better chance of winning more seats."
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said PH had a realistic opportunity to spring a surprise in Melaka.
"The BN-Pas electoral understanding gives them a significant advantage in terms of grassroots machinery, Malay voter support and electoral momentum.
"But cooperation does not automatically guarantee a complete transfer of votes between their supporters."
He said PH needed to consolidate its traditional support while attracting undecided and moderate voters, particularly in marginal and mixed constituencies.
"A surprise is possible, but it would require PH to translate dissatisfaction with the political status quo into meaningful gains."
He added that young and undecided voters could play an important role, especially in closely contested seats.
"Issues such as the cost of living, employment opportunities, housing affordability and government accountability could influence their decisions."

He said dissatisfaction with economic conditions would not automatically translate into support for PH, as some voters could hold the coalition accountable for unresolved challenges in its role in the federal government.
He said PH should prioritise competitive constituencies, such as Pengkalan Batu and Duyong, while defending Ayer Keroh, Bukit Katil, Kesidang, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, which it won in 2021.
PH's challenge in rural Malay constituencies was to overcome the perception that BN and Pas better represent Malay-Muslim interests, he added.

"PH should focus on economic security, rural development, agricultural assistance and equitable governance, while strengthening the credibility of Malay leaders from PKR and Amanah. Protecting Malay-Muslim interests and maintaining Malaysia's multiracial political framework are not mutually exclusive."
The Election Commission has set Nov 10 for nomination day, Nov 14 for polling day and Oct 31 for early voting.
Melaka has 28 state seats, with a simple majority requiring at least 15 seats and a two-thirds majority requiring 19 seats.
In the 2021 Melaka election, BN won 21 seats, allowing it to form the state government. PH won five seats, four of which went to DAP, while Perikatan Nasional secured two.

6de0dc95f0c5083a: PETALING JAYA: An activist has proposed a five-tier support system to help homeless people transition from temporary shelter to independent living, as the government reviews existing homeless outreach operations.

Yayasan Chow Kit founder Hartini Zainudin said the model, inspired by shelter and reintegration programmes in New York, would provide progressively greater support as individuals achieved goals set with their support providers.
“We focus too much on getting people off the streets and too little on understanding why they ended up there," she told FMT.
Under the proposal, the first two tiers would address immediate needs such as shelter, healthcare and documentation, before moving on to counselling, skills training and personalised planning.

The remaining tiers would focus on helping individuals secure employment, maintain stable housing and achieve financial independence, ultimately supporting their long-term integration into the community.

Hartini's proposal comes after federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh called for a review of homeless outreach operations conducted over the past three years to identify gaps in assistance and prevent those helped off the streets from becoming homeless again.

Hartini also proposed a matched-savings scheme under which participants would receive an additional RM100 for every RM100 saved from earned income, up to a specified limit, to help cover rental deposits or build emergency savings.
"The central distinction is that tiers determine additional opportunities and incentives, not whether a person deserves basic assistance," she said.
Hartini said Malaysia’s current approach to homelessness was fragmented, with limited coordination among welfare agencies, local authorities, healthcare providers and NGOs.
She called for greater emphasis on preventing homelessness and for people with lived experience of homelessness to be involved in designing support programmes.

Meanwhile, Khazanah Research Institute research associate K Theebalakshmi called for a rights-based approach to homelessness, arguing that Malaysia should recognise adequate housing as a basic human right rather than focus primarily on temporary shelter.
“In Malaysia, the right to adequate housing is not explicitly recognised as a fundamental right in the Federal Constitution,” she said.

She also called for Malaysia to rethink its social protection system, which currently centres on cash transfers and social insurance schemes, saying it must include housing support for vulnerable groups.
“Social housing can be recognised as a form of social protection that provides a safety net for vulnerable groups, including those at risk of or experiencing homelessness,” she said.

Theebalakshmi said this would require expanding access to secure tenancy and affordable rental housing, alongside job opportunities, healthcare and income assistance to help people maintain stable accommodation.
b394dcf9c339a70a: PETALING JAYA: Seorang aktivis mencadangkan sistem sokongan lima peringkat membantu gelandangan beralih daripada tempat perlindungan sementara kepada kehidupan berdikari ketika kerajaan sedang menyemak semula operasi bantuan golongan itu.

Pengasas Yayasan Chow Kit, Hartini Zainudin, merujuk model pusat perlindungan dan reintegrasi di New York yang dilihat memberikan sokongan bertahap, mengikut kejayaan individu mencapai sasaran ditetapkan bersama penyedia sokongan mereka.
“Kita terlalu beri tumpuan mengeluarkan orang ramai dari jalanan dan kurang memahami punca mereka berakhir di situ,” katanya kepada FMT.

Di bawah cadangan itu, dua peringkat pertama akan menangani keperluan mendesak seperti tempat perlindungan, penjagaan kesihatan, dan pendaftaran dokumen, sebelum beralih kepada kaunseling, latihan kemahiran, dan perancangan peribadi.

Peringkat seterusnya akan memberi tumpuan membantu mereka mendapatkan pekerjaan, mengekalkan kediaman yang stabil, dan mencapai kebebasan kewangan, seterusnya menyokong integrasi jangka panjang dalam masyarakat.

Cadangan Hartini susulan kenyataan Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Wilayah Persekutuan) Hannah Yeoh, menyeru operasi bantuan gelandangan dijalankan sejak tiga tahun lalu disemak untuk mengenal pasti jurang bantuan, selain mengelak mereka dibantu kembali menjadi bergelandangan.

Hartini turut mencadangkan skim simpanan padanan di mana peserta akan menerima RM100 tambahan bagi setiap RM100 yang disimpan daripada pendapatan kerja mereka sehingga mencapai had ditetapkan, bagi membantu menampung deposit sewa atau membina simpanan kecemasan.
“Perbezaan terasnya ialah peringkat-peringkat ini menentukan peluang dan insentif tambahan, bukannya menentukan sama ada seseorang itu layak menerima bantuan asas atau tidak,” katanya.

Hartini berkata, pendekatan Malaysia terhadap isu gelandangan pada masa ini seperti berkecamuk dengan penyelarasan yang terhad antara agensi kebajikan, pihak berkuasa tempatan, penyedia perkhidmatan kesihatan, dan NGO.
Beliau menggesa penekanan lebih besar diberikan kepada usaha mencegah masalah gelandangan dengan individu mempunyai pengalaman hidup gelandangan dilibatkan dalam mereka bentuk program sokongan.

Sementara itu, penyelidik bersekutu Institut Penyelidikan Khazanah, K Theebalakshmi, menyeru pendekatan berasaskan hak terhadap gelandangan sambil menyatakan Malaysia patut mengiktiraf kediaman wajar sebagai hak asasi, bukan ke atas tempat perlindungan sementara sahaja.
“Di Malaysia, hak kepada kediaman wajar tidak diiktiraf secara jelas sebagai hak asasi dalam Perlembagaan Persekutuan,” katanya.

Beliau mencadangkan Malaysia meneliti semula sistem perlindungan sosialnya, yang ketika ini menumpukan kepada bantuan tunai dan skim insurans sosial, selain mesti merangkumi sokongan perumahan bagi kumpulan rentan.

“Perumahan sosial boleh diiktiraf sebagai satu bentuk perlindungan sosial yang menyediakan jaring keselamatan bagi kumpulan rentan, termasuk mereka berisiko atau sedang mengalami masalah gelandangan,” katanya.

Theebalakshmi berkata, perkara itu memerlukan perluasan akses sewaan yang terjamin dan perumahan sewa mampu milik, disekali pekerjaan, penjagaan kesihatan, dan bantuan pendapatan membantu mereka terus mempunyai kediaman.
b3405e685a74f74e: MELAKA: When Hassan Faisal Sayujan looked at the old copper moulds his grandparents had used to make bahulu in the 1980s, he saw more than ageing kitchen equipment.
They were still usable, and with them came the possibility of reviving a family tradition that had gradually faded as his grandparents grew older.
About three years ago, Hassan Faisal, 37, left a stable job in the manufacturing sector in Kuala Lumpur and began making traditional kuih bahulu full-time.
He now runs the business with his father-in-law, Iskandar Nor Baharom, while his wife, Nurul Syamimi Iskandar Nor, is also involved.

“My grandparents started making bahulu traditionally in Kuala Pilah in 1982, using copper moulds and coconut husks to bake the cakes. However, they eventually had to stop due to their age,” he told Bernama.

“I am the third generation to carry on the business, together with my father-in-law. We initially did it to earn some extra money, selling bahulu online and at booths and carnivals around KL. We never expected our bahulu to be in such high demand.”

Elaborating, he said the venture actually began in 2018 as a weekend sideline. As orders grew, the family set up a dedicated workshop in Kuala Pilah in late 2023, followed by an outlet in Melaka in August 2024.
While a third outlet in Temerloh is due to open at the end of this month, Hassan Faisal said expansion has not changed the way the cakes are made.

Instead of a modern oven, the bahulu is baked using copper moulds heated over a gas stove, with coconut husks placed above them. A blower is used to keep the heat moving evenly through the baking process.
“Unlike modern ovens, where the temperature can be adjusted at the touch of a button, our method uses a gas stove, with coconut husks placed on top of the copper mould,” he said.
“We prefer the moulds because copper retains heat for longer. So, even when the heat from the burning coconut husks begins to die down, the mould remains hot.”
That method demands judgement: too much heat can burn the cakes, while too little can affect their texture. The bakers have to learn how to read the fire and the moulds as they work.
Preserving the method comes with another difficulty: finding people willing to learn it. The work is hot and smoky, and staff spend long periods standing close to the baking area.
Hassan Faisal said these conditions can make it harder to attract younger workers, even as interest in traditional food remains strong.

The business now employs 14 people, with production carried out in both Kuala Pilah and Melaka. The Melaka outlet alone can produce at least 100 containers of bahulu a day, in original and pandan flavours.
If the baking process is rooted in tradition, the way customers find the baulu is decidedly modern: online sales, particularly through TikTok, account for about 60-70% of the business.
Their team also livestreams daily from the Kuala Pilah workshop, giving viewers a look at how the traditional cakes are made.
That contrast has become part of the story: an old family recipe and decades-old equipment - reaching customers through smartphones and livestreams.

aece5487e31935d9: NEW MEXICO: A Utah judge on Friday said he needed more time to decide when to start the trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk more than a year ago, media reported.

At a hearing in Provo, Utah, District Court Judge Tony Graf heard arguments from defence lawyers, prosecutors and a lawyer for Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, before saying he needed to consider their positions. He set a new hearing for November 9, television station KUTV reported.

Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to seven counts, including aggravated murder, for allegedly shooting Kirk as he held one of his trademark debates at Utah Valley University in Orem. Robinson's lawyers expect a six-to-seven-month trial.

Robinson's attorneys had asked for a trial in late 2029 to give them time to challenge Utah's request for the death penalty, gather additional evidence and seek a change of venue, among other issues, according to a scheduling memo.
Prosecutors, meanwhile, sought a date of Jan 31, 2028, to start what they expect to be a 17-week trial, according to their scheduling memo.
In a separate filing, Erika Kirk said the defence request was "grossly out of line with comparable cases" and requested that the trial start no later than Oct 4, 2027.

Shortly before Friday's hearing, President Donald Trump, with whom Kirk had been allied, criticised Graf's handling of the case in a social media post, saying it should be tried within a month and that Graf was asking "questions that people already know the answer to".

Kirk was a polarising figure in US politics. He was admired by conservatives for mobilising young voters around his Christian and right-wing views. Opponents criticised his rhetoric on immigration, race, gender and other social issues.
Prosecutors allege Robinson targeted Kirk because of his opposition to gay marriage and transgender rights.

Defence attorney Richard Novak has said Kirk spoke "hatefully" about people who did not have traditional gender identities or were not heterosexual, but there was no evidence Robinson opposed those views.
d1d98e125fdcbdea: LISBON: Thailand welcomes US engagement with Myanmar and expects discussions at the Asean summit in Manila on how to proceed with the member barred since the 2021 coup, foreign minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told Reuters on Friday.
The US and Myanmar's military-backed government held talks in Tokyo two weeks ago, their second meeting in a month as Washington steps up re-engagement with the generals it shunned after the coup.
"We don't want to see Myanmar isolated, we don't want Myanmar to be an arena for geopolitical rivalry ... so the US engagement is something that we welcome," he said.
Engagement "does not mean legitimising the regime," but aims to encourage peaceful conflict resolution and reconciliation with the opposition, Sihasak, who is also deputy prime minister, added.

He said there was "some shift in Asean's position," citing Myanmar president Min Aung Hlaing's recent visits to Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia, but said it was unclear whether the Manila summit would address restoring Myanmar's full representation.
"It's good that we're going to have a very substantive, very extensive, and very in-depth discussion on how to proceed on Myanmar," he said.
He also said Thailand and Cambodia could resolve their longstanding land and maritime boundary disputes within 12 to 18 months despite limited progress.
"It is possible, everything is possible," he said, cautioning that confidence-building and addressing security concerns along the land border, where clashes have occurred, must come first.

Cambodia launched a conciliation process under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea in June to resolve the maritime boundary dispute, after Thailand terminated a 2001 joint development framework in May following deadly border clashes. The first meeting was held about a month ago.
"Right now, we haven't achieved, to be very frank, much progress," he said.

The maritime dispute centers on overlapping claims to about 26,000 sq km in the Gulf of Thailand, believed to hold oil and gas reserves worth around US$300 billion. Thailand wants the boundary defined before discussing resource-sharing, he said.
Thailand-EU free-trade talks are in their final stage and could conclude by year-end if there is mutual political will, he added.
d9bc1cf2c4a2f50b: KUALA LUMPUR: Civil servants are seeking clarity over the decision to ban them from using the Waze navigation application. This includes the government's concerns over the app's alleged links to Israel and the security of users' location data.

A civil servant, who spoke on condition of anonymity, asked why the ban was not extended to all users if the government was concerned that location data could be exposed to the Israeli government or companies.
"Ordinary Malaysians are also using Waze and their location data could be exposed, too. If it is a security threat to the country, then it should be a blanket ban.
"But if the concern is only about government operations, the government should explain why the restriction is necessary for all civil servants," he said.
He added that if the Waze ban was on national security grounds, then it should focus only on sensitive government bodies, including the Prime Minister's Office, Home Ministry and Defence Ministry.
"Their movements and activities may involve sensitive matters, so there is a stronger reason to take precautions there."
He said it was unfair to single out civil servants as the app was still available for use by other Malaysians.
On Wednesday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered civil servants to stop using Waze over concerns that sensitive government information and personal data could be exploited by Israel.
However, Anwar said yesterday the government had not ruled out imposing a nationwide ban on Waze once suitable alternatives became available.
"I will not allow civil servants to use it under any circumstances. Waze is banned.
"We need to study the available alternatives. If we find that their capabilities are sufficiently developed, we may consider using the facilities available."

Anwar said Malaysians should switch to locally developed alternatives such as TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, citing assurances over data security and personal information protection.
Another civil servant asked why United States-based apps such as Google Maps, Instagram and WhatsApp remained accessible.
"Why is Waze banned while Google Maps is available? Both are used for navigation and require location data."
She added that Instagram and WhatsApp should also be considered when the government assessed the potential exposure of personal information to foreign companies.
"If the concern is about foreign companies collecting data, then the government needs to explain the criteria it uses.
"Otherwise, people will question why one application is banned while other widely used apps remain accessible."
Another civil servant questioned whether disciplinary action would be taken if a civil servant was found using Waze.

"We are expected to follow government instructions, but there must also be a clear explanation why this decision was made. If the concern is national security, then explain to us what the concern is and why Waze is singled out," she said.
Civil servants have been warned that they would face disciplinary action if found using the app, with department heads overseeing compliance with the directive.
Asked whether any spot checks had been conducted in her department, she said: "So far, there have been no checks to see whether we have downloaded TuJu and uninstalled Waze.
"We have received instructions from the top management reminding us to comply with the Waze directive and not make any comments on social media, particularly those that belittle TuJu."

She also questioned whether the government had properly considered the alternatives available to those who rely on Waze for their travel needs, saying her experience with TuJu had raised concerns over its reliability.
"I searched for my home address but the app displayed the message: 'No results found, try searching with different keywords'.
"The same thing happened when I tried searching for Dataran Merdeka. If the app cannot even find this location, how reliable is it as an alternative to Waze?"
She said navigation apps were not just about finding the direction to a destination, but also providing accurate locations and convenient routes, particularly for those unfamiliar with an area.
She added that civil servants would need an alternative that could meet their daily needs, including travelling to meetings, attending official functions and finding unfamiliar addresses.
"If we are told to stop using Waze immediately, then the alternative should at least work properly.
"Otherwise, it will be difficult for users who depend on navigation apps to get around."

e773fb082e591028: PETALING JAYA: Former Malaysian Armed Forces captain Norisham Kadmin’s business has weathered numerous challenges over the years.
In 2010, after more than a decade in military service, he ventured into the batik industry with just RM500 in capital.
The journey was far from smooth. Norisham’s business faced multiple challenges, including fires, floods and the Covid-19 pandemic, which almost brought operations to a standstill.

In 2023, during one of the company’s most challenging periods, the National Entrepreneurial Group Economic Fund (Tekun Nasional) provided RM100,000 in financing, helping Norisham sustain the business he had spent more than a decade building.
“My business was at the point of needing CPR. It was then that Tekun came and helped revive it.

“Tekun did not only give us financing. They took an interest in our situation and invited us to enrol in courses and visit expos. They always help entrepreneurs grow,” the managing director of Batik House Sdn Bhd told FMT.

An agency under the entrepreneur development and cooperatives ministry (Kuskop), Tekun provides microfinancing and development support to entrepreneurs, and Norisham's story is one of its many successes.
Two other entrepreneurs also credited the agency with helping them navigate setbacks, particularly during periods when they struggled to secure funding from other financial institutions.
Capital as a point of change
Vision Automotive Technology Sdn Bhd managing director R Samanan’s dream of starting his own workshop came from his father, who wanted to see him succeed in the automotive industry.
Samanan established Vision Automotive in 2003 and secured RM50,000 in financing from Tekun a decade later, helping to drive the expansion of his company’s operations.
In 2017, he received another RM80,000 in financing, which he used to purchase business premises.
“That working capital was what changed the course of our company. From there, we grew little by little,” he said.
Tekun, the ‘university of life’
For Neuronworks International Serantau Bhd founder and CEO Rizal Rashid, Tekun holds special meaning, having been employed by the agency before transitioning to entrepreneurship.

Relocating from Kota Kinabalu to Peninsular Malaysia more than 26 years ago, he was inspired to venture into business after witnessing firsthand how Tekun helped entrepreneurs grow and expand their ventures.

Rizal set up Neuronworks in 2015, expanding his career as a motivation and communications expert. He received RM50,000 in financing, followed by another RM100,000 based on his strong repayment record.

He used the financing to set up a training facility and expand his company’s operations, successfully training more than 70,000 people so far, including entrepreneurs, professionals, civil servants, influencers and politicians.
“Tekun has been my ‘university of life’. I saw many entrepreneurs benefit from their help, and wanted to become one of them myself,” he said.
Documents at one’s fingertips
All three entrepreneurs welcomed measures introduced by Kuskop under its minister Steven Sim to improve access to financing for business owners.
They said the initiatives, including the launch of the Tekun Online Application System this year, have made it easier for entrepreneurs to apply for financing.

Thanks to enhancements to its approval process, applications for microfinancing of up to RM20,000 can now be approved within 24 hours, while those for up to RM100,000 may be approved within seven days of full document submission.
Norisham described the improvements as a positive step towards speeding up the financing process for entrepreneurs.
“I thought it was very good, because it has reduced bureaucracy. This faster approval system will make things easier for entrepreneurs.
“More importantly, Tekun continues to be with us — through courses, expos and guidance,” he said.
Samanan said the current application process is much simpler than it was when he applied for financing more than a decade ago. “Back then, everything was manual.
The documents were thick. Now everything is online,” he said.
Besides easing the application process, the government has stepped up support for entrepreneurs by allocating RM1 billion in financing to Bumiputera entrepreneurs this year.
The allocation for the Indian Community Entrepreneur Development Scheme (Spumi) was also increased from RM75 million to RM120 million this year.
Partners in entrepreneur development

Norisham, Samanan and Rizal’s stories show that while every business faces different challenges, access to financing and appropriate guidance can help entrepreneurs sustain and expand their operations.

In line with reforms introduced under Sim's leadership, Tekun continues to strengthen its role as more than just a financing provider, supporting entrepreneur development through training, mentorship and innovations such as its digital application system.
For Rizal, the agency’s continued support has boosted entrepreneurs’ confidence.
“Tekun does not just provide financing. They care for entrepreneur development and give us confidence to move further,” he said.
Expanded financing and easier processes
Since Sim took over Kuskop in December last year, Tekun has introduced a raft of reforms to speed up application processing and expand access to financing for more microentrepreneurs.
In August 2026, the agency launched its Tekun Online Application System 2026, allowing entrepreneurs to apply for financing entirely online.

Processing times have also been significantly reduced, with approval periods for financing of up to RM100,000 substantially shortened. As of July 2026, 74.5% of nearly 31,000 approved financing applications were processed within one to five days.
Allocations have also been increased substantially.
Funding for Bumiputera entrepreneurs rose from RM300 million to RM500 million in 2025, before being doubled to RM1 billion this year.
Meanwhile, financing for Indian entrepreneurs under Spumi has seen an increase, from RM75 million to RM120 million between 2025 and 2026.
Financing support has also been expanded to help small businesses prepare for major festive seasons.

The BARAKAT Ramadan scheme was introduced with RM50 million in funding to assist traders ahead of Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidilfitri, while BERKAT Deepavali provides working capital to Indian entrepreneurs preparing for the festival.
c67850155ad42f9e: PETALING JAYA: Bermula dengan modal hanya RM500, bekas kapten Angkatan Tentera Malaysia (ATM), Norisham Kadmin, membina perniagaannya sebelum berdepan pelbagai musibah termasuk kebakaran, banjir besar dan pandemik Covid-19 yang hampir melumpuhkan operasinya.
Selepas lebih sedekad berkhidmat dalam ATM, Norisham, 51, memilih bidang keusahawanan dan mula menceburi industri batik sekitar 2010.
Ketika perniagaannya berdepan kesukaran, pembiayaan kira-kira RM100,000 daripada Tekun Nasional pada 2023 membantunya meneruskan perniagaan yang dibina sejak lebih sedekad lalu.
“Saya fikir perniagaan ini sudah sampai saat perlu diberi 'CPR'. Ketika itulah Tekun datang membantu menghidupkan semula perniagaan kami,” kata pengarah urusan Batik House Sdn Bhd itu kepada FMT.
“Tekun bukan sekadar bagi pinjaman, mereka ambil tahu keadaan kita, jemput ke kursus, ekspo dan sentiasa bantu usahawan berkembang,” katanya.
Tekun Nasional agensi di bawah Kementerian Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi (Kuskop) yang menyediakan pembiayaan mikro serta sokongan pembangunan kepada usahawan.
Pengalaman Norisham antara tiga kisah usahawan daripada latar belakang dan industri berbeza yang mendapat manfaat daripada pembiayaan dan bimbingan Tekun.

Walaupun berdepan cabaran berbeza, ketiga-tiganya berkongsi pengalaman mendapat sokongan Tekun untuk meneruskan dan mengembangkan perniagaan ketika akses kepada pembiayaan daripada institusi kewangan lain tidak mudah diperoleh.
Modal jadi titik perubahan
Bagi Pengarah Urusan Vision Automotive Technology Sdn Bhd, R Samanan, hasrat membina bengkel sendiri bermula daripada impian bapanya yang mahu melihat beliau berjaya dalam bidang automotif.
Berbekalkan pengalaman dalam industri itu, Samanan menubuhkan Vision Automotive pada 2003 sebelum memperoleh pembiayaan RM50,000 daripada Tekun pada 2013.
Pembiayaan itu menjadi pemangkin untuk mengembangkan operasi syarikatnya.
Empat tahun kemudian, beliau menerima pembiayaan tambahan RM80,000 pada 2017 yang digunakan untuk membeli premis perniagaan sendiri.
“Pusingan modal itulah yang mengubah perjalanan syarikat kami. Dari situ kami berkembang sedikit demi sedikit,” katanya.
Tekun universiti kehidupan

Bagi pengasas dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Neuronworks International Serantau Berhad, Mohd Rizal Rashid, Tekun mempunyai makna tersendiri kerana beliau pernah berkhidmat dengan agensi itu sebelum menceburi bidang keusahawanan.

Berhijrah dari Kota Kinabalu ke Semenanjung lebih 26 tahun lalu, pengalaman bekerja dengan Tekun memberinya keyakinan untuk memulakan perniagaan sendiri selepas menyaksikan ramai usahawan mendapat manfaat daripada bantuan agensi berkenaan.

Beliau kemudian menubuhkan Neuronworks pada 2015 dan mengembangkan kerjaya sebagai pakar motivasi dan komunikasi sebelum menerima pembiayaan RM50,000 daripada Tekun, diikuti pembiayaan tambahan RM100,000 berdasarkan rekod bayaran balik yang baik.

Pembiayaan itu digunakan untuk melengkapkan fasiliti latihan dan mengembangkan operasi syarikatnya yang kini berjaya melatih lebih 70,000 individu, termasuk usahawan, profesional, penjawat awam, pempengaruh dan ahli politik.
“Tekun ialah universiti kehidupan saya. Saya melihat ramai usahawan berjaya dibantu dan akhirnya saya sendiri mahu menjadi sebahagian daripada mereka,” katanya.
Dulu dokumen tebal, kini di hujung jari
Ketiga-tiga usahawan itu turut menyambut baik pembaharuan yang diperkenalkan Kuskop di bawah kepimpinan Menteri Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi, Steven Sim, bagi memudahkan akses kepada pembiayaan.
Antara inisiatif tersebut ialah pelancaran Sistem Tekun Online tahun ini yang membolehkan usahawan membuat permohonan pembiayaan sepenuhnya secara dalam talian.

Menerusi penambahbaikan proses kelulusan, pembiayaan mikro sehingga RM20,000 bakal diluluskan seawal 24 jam, manakala pembiayaan sehingga RM100,000 seawal tujuh hari bekerja selepas dokumen lengkap diterima.
Norisham menyifatkan pembaharuan itu sebagai langkah positif untuk mengurangkan birokrasi dan mempercepatkan proses pembiayaan kepada usahawan.
“Apabila saya dapat tahu Kuskop di bawah Steven Sim memperkenalkan kelulusan seawal tujuh hari, saya fikir ia satu pembaharuan yang sangat baik kerana dapat mengurangkan birokrasi,” katanya.
"Sistem kelulusan yang lebih pantas ini memudahkan usahawan. Lebih penting, Tekun terus bersama kita melalui kursus, ekspo dan bimbingan," katanya.
Samanan pula berkata, proses permohonan kini jauh lebih mudah berbanding ketika beliau mendapatkan pembiayaan lebih sedekad lalu.
"Dulu masa saya mohon, semuanya masih manual. Dokumen pun tebal macam ini. Sekarang dah 'online'," katanya.
Selain memudahkan proses permohonan, kerajaan turut meningkatkan sokongan kepada usahawan menerusi peruntukan pembiayaan RM1 bilion kepada usahawan mikro Bumiputera tahun ini melalui Tekun.
Peruntukan Skim Pembangunan Usahawan Masyarakat India (SPUMI) turut dinaikkan daripada RM75 juta tahun lalu kepada RM120 juta tahun ini.
Bukan sekadar modal tetapi rakan pembangunan usahawan

Kisah Norisham, Samanan dan Rizal menunjukkan walaupun cabaran setiap perniagaan berbeza, akses kepada pembiayaan dan bimbingan yang bersesuaian mampu membantu usahawan meneruskan serta mengembangkan operasi mereka.

Seiring pembaharuan yang diperkenalkan Kuskop di bawah kepimpinan Sim, Tekun terus memperkukuh peranannya bukan sekadar sebagai penyedia pembiayaan, malah sebagai rakan pembangunan usahawan menerusi latihan, bimbingan dan pelaksanaan sistem permohonan dalam talian.
Bagi Rizal, yang pernah menjadi kakitangan Tekun sebelum menerima pembiayaa untuk mengembangkan syarikatnya sendiri, sokongan berterusan agensi itu turut memberi keyakinan kepada usahawan.
"Tekun bukan sekadar menyediakan modal. Mereka sentiasa mengambil berat perkembangan usahawan dan memberi keyakinan untuk kami terus melangkah lebih jauh," katanya.

Pembiayaan diperluas, proses dipermudah Sejak Sim menerajui Kuskop pada Disember 2025, beberapa pembaharuan dan inisiatif diperkenalkan melalui Tekun Nasional bagi mempercepatkan proses permohonan serta memperluas akses pembiayaan kepada usahawan mikro.

Permohonan secara dalam talian: Buat pertama kali dalam sejarah hampir 30 tahun penubuhannya, Tekun melancarkan Sistem Tekun Online pada Ogos 2026, membolehkan usahawan memohon pembiayaan sepenuhnya secara dalam talian.

Kelulusan lebih pantas: Tempoh pemprosesan pembiayaan sehingga RM100,000 dipendekkan daripada kira-kira 30 hari kepada tujuh hari bekerja. Bagi pembiayaan mikro sehingga RM20,000, Tekun sedang berusaha mencapai sasaran kelulusan seawal 24 jam selepas dokumen lengkap diterima. Sehingga Julai 2026, sebanyak 74.5% daripada hampir 31,000 pembiayaan yang diluluskan mendapat kelulusan dalam tempoh satu hingga lima hari.
Pembiayaan Bumiputera: Peruntukan ditingkatkan daripada RM300 juta pada 2025 kepada RM500 juta, sebelum dinaikkan lagi kepada RM1 bilion pada 2026.
Pembiayaan usahawan India: Peruntukan SPUMI ditingkatkan daripada RM75 juta pada 2025 kepada RM120 juta pada 2026.

Pembiayaan musim perayaan: Skim Barakat Ramadan diperkenalkan dengan dana RM50 juta bagi membantu peniaga menjelang Ramadan dan Aidilfitri, manakala Berkat Deepavali menyediakan modal pusingan kepada usahawan India menjelang perayaan.

8cf72eaf3ce083d1: MCBA chief and former Temerloh police chief charged in separate cases

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain made headlines after becoming the first high-ranking officer of the agency to be charged with assaulting two Special Branch policemen.
Shuhaily, 54, appeared calm as he faced two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to lance corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, 25, and Mohamad Faiz Saman, 40.

He appeared before magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani at the Sepang court complex, about three weeks after a video allegedly showing him assaulting the duo, who are travel control officers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
If convicted under Section 323 of the Penal Code, Shuhaily faces a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
He was released after a family friend posted bail of RM1,500 with one surety for each charge. He is set to return to court for case management on Nov 25.
Below are the other major court cases this week
FORMER TEMERLOH POLICE CHIEF JAILED FOR BRIBERY

On Wednesday, former Temerloh police chief Superintendent Mohd Azhar Mohd Yusoff was sentenced to eight months in jail after being found guilty of 46 counts of accepting bribes totalling RM69,600 between 2019 and 2023.

Temerloh Sessions Court judge Sazlina Safie ruled that the 56-year-old failed to raise reasonable doubt over the prosecution's case that he had received the money through online transfers into his bank account over nearly four years and had abused his authority for personal gain.

The court rejected a plea by his lawyer, Datuk M. Athimulan, for a fine instead of jail, arguing that the conviction itself could cost his client his job, pension and other benefits accumulated throughout his 36-years service.
Azhar was granted a stay of execution pending appeal, with the court increasing his bail by RM5,000 to RM30,000.
JOVIAN LOSES APPEALS

On Tuesday, the Court of Appeal dismissed fashion designer Datuk Jovian Mandagie's appeals against summary judgments obtained by Bina Pragmatik Sdn Bhd and Cekap Air Sdn Bhd in a 2-1 majority decision.
The ruling upheld the High Court decisions ordering Jovian to repay RM10 million in alleged friendly loans from the two companies, together with RM60,000 in costs.

Judge Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, who chaired the panel, and Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril found that Jovian had failed to provide sufficient evidence to support his claim that the money was intended as business investments rather than loans.
However, dissenting judge Datin Evrol Mariette Peters said the transfer of money into law firms' client accounts did not, in itself, establish that the payments were loans.

She also noted that neither company had produced contemporaneous written documents establishing the alleged loan agreements, while the letters of demand issued to Jovian did not refer to the purported arrangements.
COUPLE SENT TO THE GALLOWS
A couple known as Ah Long Harimau was sentenced to death by the Federal Court for murdering 38-year-old Heng Heow Lin in Sibu, Sarawak in 2020, over a RM800 debt.
Judges Datuk Azizah Nawawi, Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang and Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah unanimously dismissed the final appeal of Seow Pei Chee and her husband Cheung Chia Ming, both 44.
The court heard that the victim was repeatedly abused and strangled before her body was stuffed into luggage and dumped by the roadside over the debt.
The couple had pushed Heng and her daughter into prostitution, kept the earnings and assaulted them when their collection was too little.
TYCOON CLAIMS TRIAL OVER RM10 MILLION CHEATING CHARGES

Businessman Tan Sri Tan Kean Soon, 63, pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court to four counts of cheating fellow businessman Datuk Seri Keh Chuan Seng, 55, of RM10 million by allegedly misleading him into believing he could resolve issues involving frozen bank accounts and a police investigation linked to money laundering.
Tan allegedly induced Keh to hand over RM2 million, RM3 million, S$1.5 million and RM500,000 through Datuk Seri Chiau Beng Teik.
The charges, under Section 420 of the Penal Code, carry imprisonment of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Judge Azrul Darus granted Tan bail of RM1 million with one surety, despite the prosecution's objection to bail given the non-bailable nature of the offence and the RM10 million involved.
TERESA KOK WINS DEFAMATION SUIT AGAINST AKMAL, AWARDED RM250,000

Seputeh member of parliament Teresa Kok won her defamation suit against Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh at the Melaka High Court on Oct 19 over his remarks aimed at her on the country's halal certification issue.
Judicial Commissioner Datuk Isa Aziz Ibrahim ordered Akmal to pay RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages as well as RM50,000 in costs.

In the 2024 suit, Kok claimed Akmal had defamed her in two articles published on a news portal, titled "Akmal: Saya Minta Kerajaan Sediakan Logo Non-Halal, Tampal Pada Dahi Teresa" and "UMNO Youth Chief swipes at 'old Nyonya' Teresa over halal cert".

The court also ordered Akmal to remove the video from his social media accounts within seven days and permanently restrained him from republishing the defamatory statements or words to the same effect.
PAPAGOMO FREED ONCE AGAIN, A-GC TO APPEAL
Blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, has been acquitted and discharged for the second time over alleged remarks that the government was pro-Israel.
The 43-year-old was freed by Sessions Court judge Siti Aminah Ghazali at the end of the defence case on Monday, after she found that the defence had raised reasonable doubt in the prosecution's case.
She had previously freed Wan Azri at the close of the prosecution's case before the High Court remitted the case back to Siti Aminah after ruling that a prima facie had been established.
However, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has decided to appeal against the acquittal, setting the stage for another round of legal proceedings.
He was charged with making the allegedly seditious remarks on the Facebook page of Halid Hamidi at 1pm on Nov 8, 2023.
The charge framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948, carries a maximum fine of RM5,000, a jail term of up to three years, or both upon conviction.
LEE ZII JIA SETTLES FAMILY DISPUTE, COMPANY TO HOLD EGM
Professional shuttler Lee Zii Jia drew attention at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Tuesday when he appeared for mediation over a family dispute involving his company, LZJ Management Sdn Bhd.
The dispute was resolved through an amicable settlement, with High Court judge Leong Wai Hong recording a consent judgment on Oct 20.
Under the agreement, the company must hold an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Oct 31, with the costs to be borne by the company.

Pending the meeting, Lee's father, Lee Chee Hin, 59, and elder sister, Lee Zii Yii, 30, are restrained from approving or authorising directors' fees, allowances, bonuses or other financial benefits for themselves, apart from their monthly salaries.
They are also barred from making decisions that could materially affect the company's management, administration or control without prior court approval.

Lee, 28, filed the originating summons on July 2, naming LZJ Management, his father, sister and younger brother, Lee Tao, 25, as respondents. The court made no order as to costs, following the settlement between the parties.

fbb2668a818ca36e: WASHINGTON: The US transportation department (USDOT) said Friday it was fining Air France and KLM a total of US$425,000 for operating dozens of flights in Iraqi airspace below a minimum altitude intended to protect them from threats from the ground.

The Federal Aviation Administration prohibits flight operations by US operators in foreign-managed airspace where conflict, militant activity, or heightened tensions can threaten the safety of flights. Foreign airlines operating flights with a US airline’s code must abide by these prohibitions, and KLM and Air France both operate flights with Delta codes.
An FAA order in place for more than six years bars flights over Iraq at altitudes below 32,000 feet.
Air France operated more than 30 flights and KLM more than 100 flights carrying the Delta code through FAA-prohibited airspace over Iraq between early 2022 and 2025, USDOT said.
USDOT said the airlines must pay US$265,000 of the US$425,000 within 60 days and the remainder of the fines will be payable if there are any other violations within one year.
The airlines did not immediately comment but Air France and KLM told USDOT they were fully committed to adhering to regulatory requirements at all times and took the issue extremely seriously.
Both airlines said that due to conflicting traffic, local air traffic controllers had directly instructed their flight crews to descend or refused to allow them to ascend.
Both said they believe the flights should have fallen under the “emergency situations” exemption given the safety implications of refusing an air traffic control order.
66cec0464a3d0334: KUALA LUMPUR: Murder, violence, organised crime and shocking attacks dominated Malaysia's crime headlines this week, with several cases drawing widespread public attention and raising concerns over safety and security.

From the murder of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer at a government residential complex in Nilai to an alleged attack on a teacher by a Form Four student at an international school in Kuching, the cases highlighted the range and severity of crimes being investigated by police.
Here are some of the cases that made headlines this week:
MCBA officer found dead at quarters, husband remanded
The murder of MCBA officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, remained one of the week's most closely followed cases after she was found dead at a government residential complex in Nilai on Oct 15.
A post-mortem found that she died from pressure on the neck, while stab wounds were also detected on the side of her abdomen and cheek.
Her husband, in his 30s, was detained after surrendering at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang.
Police have recorded statements from 18 people to assist investigations.
The suspect was remanded for seven days to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Police also revealed that the suspect had 16 previous criminal records, including 10 involving narcotics offences and six relating to housebreaking, theft and possession of stolen property.
Student attacks teacher with axe at Kuching school
A 16-year-old Form Four student was arrested after attacking a female teacher at an international school in Kuching on Wednesday.
The incident occurred at 7.49am, with police confirming that the teacher suffered an injury to her hand.
Police seized an axe and a penknife at the scene, while reports also stated that the student had brought firecrackers to the school.
The incident quickly went viral after footage purportedly showing the attack circulated online, prompting renewed concerns over the safety of teachers and students.
School authorities said the student was restrained following the incident before police were alerted.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident, including the motive for the attack.
Geng Suria linked to 20 violent and property crimes busted
Bukit Aman announced they had busted an organised crime group known as Geng Suria, which is believed to be linked to 20 property and violent crimes in Kedah.
Federal police Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the group was believed to have been active since early 2024 and comprised nine members aged between 28 and 52.
The group was allegedly led by a 30-year-old local man and targeted homes belonging to foreigners, business premises and residential properties identified by its leader.
Police said members used dangerous weapons, including knives and machetes, during robberies and did not hesitate to injure victims.
Several victims allegedly suffered serious injuries, while the group was believed to have caused losses amounting to hundreds of thousands of ringgit.
The operation, dubbed Op Sunset, was conducted by Bukit Aman CID with the Kedah contingent CID from Sept 24 to 27 in Kedah and Perak.
Six suspects were arrested, while three others were already being held at prisons in Sungai Buloh, Pokok Sena and Sungai Petani for other offences.
The nine are scheduled to be charged soon at the Sungai Petani Sessions Court for membership in an organised crime group.
Baby dies after suffering head injuries from blunt-force trauma
The death of a 10-month-old boy in Tasek Gelugor, Penang, took a more serious turn after a post-mortem found that he had suffered head injuries consistent with blunt-force trauma.
The baby was under the care of a babysitter when he was found weak and lethargic at her home on Monday morning.
The babysitter reportedly discovered the child at 9.50am before he was taken for medical treatment.
He later died, prompting police to detain the babysitter to assist investigations.
The post-mortem found that the injuries could have been fatal.
Police are continuing investigations to determine how the injuries occurred and whether a criminal element was involved.
13 held over Molotov cocktail attack on Rohingya settlement
Police arrested 13 local men, aged between 16 and 31, over an alleged Molotov cocktail attack on a Rohingya settlement in Kulai Besar, Johor.
The suspects were arrested in and around Johor Baru during a five-day operation conducted by the Johor CID between Oct 13 and 18.
Four of the suspects were found to have a combined 12 previous criminal and drug-related offences.
The attack occurred on Oct 13, when Molotov cocktails were allegedly thrown at the settlement.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack and the motive behind it.
Cross-border operation cripples online vice syndicate

A joint Malaysia-Singapore operation resulted in the arrest of 30 people over an alleged cross-border prostitution syndicate that used Malaysia as its base to offer online sex services to customers in Singapore.
The operation involved Bukit Aman and the Singapore Police Force, with raids conducted to dismantle the syndicate's operations.
Police said the group was believed to have used websites to advertise prostitution services to customers in Singapore.
Nine people wanted by Singapore police over their alleged involvement in the syndicate were also arrested in Malaysia.
The operation highlighted cross-border organised vice activities, particularly by using online platforms and exploiting the close movement of people between Malaysia and Singapore.
Investigations are continuing to establish the full structure of the syndicate and the respective roles of those detained.
